prediction: HELD-OUT PERMUTATION TEST. Fit the corner relabelling P on -1to1 ALONE, by maximising its agreement, then apply that SAME P unchanged to the other five captures and report agreement. This design exists because quoting agreement under a permutation fitted to the same capture is a tautology -- the permutation is chosen to maximise the number being quoted, so it cannot fail. Fitting on one capture and predicting five held-out ones can fail, and here is how I expect it to. I PREDICT IT IS NOT ONE PERMUTATION. The per-capture transforms already computed disagree with each other: 0to1 and HiLo_1 both imply an s flip AND a t flip, -1to1 and -1to1GL both imply a t flip ONLY, -1to1D3D implies an s flip with t mixed. So P, fitted on -1to1, is the t-flip-only transform, and it should transfer to -1to1GL and to nothing else. QUANTITATIVELY: (1) -1to1GL under P >= 60%, close to its own best of 64.5%, because it is the same transform family. (2) 0to1, HiLo_1, HiLoHemi and -1to1D3D under P all < 40%, each far below its own best (80.0, 75.6, 66.4, 91.8) -- P does not transfer to them. (3) Therefore the relabelling is PER-MAPPING, not global, which means the substitution interacts with the dotmap and the shape of the fix changes: it is not a component-order or sign-convention transposition that one constant fixes. FALSIFIER, and it is the outcome I would prefer to be true: if ALL SIX come out >= 60% under P, it IS a single global relabelling, my claim is wrong, and the fix is small -- a transposed corner encoding on top of a correct coordinate. Any capture landing between 40% and 60% is neither, and I would report the rule as undetermined rather than pick a side. NOTE THIS IS NOT BLIND: I am predicting from the per-capture transform table I already computed, so it is a forward inference from measured structure and not a guess. What makes it falsifiable anyway is that cross-applying a permutation is NOT what that table measured -- the table gave each capture its own best fit, and whether one capture's fit transfers to another is unmeasured. Tie-breaking among near-equal permutations could make it behave differently from what the table suggests. RESIDUE STRUCTURE, a second and independent question: after the BEST permutation, -1to1D3D still leaves 8.2% wrong. I predict that residue is SPATIALLY STRUCTURED rather than scattered -- measured as the mean number of 4-neighbours a residue pixel has that are also residue, against the value expected if the same count were scattered at random over the cube region (4 * |R| / |cube|). I predict observed > 2x random. Structured means the corner rule is exact with a labelling bug plus a second smaller rule on top; scattered means the corner rule is only approximate and no relabelling will finish it.
